The power of a mobile phone emitter increases when the phone is switched on. The power output of the emitter after $t$ minutes is given by $W(t),$ where $W$ is measured in watts. The graph of $W(t)$ is shown above. 
Approximate the rate of increase in the power of the emitter when $t=1$ using a forward difference approximation with step size $h=2.$

activity_context.topic_title: Estimating Derivatives Using a Forward Difference Quotient

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14057748/assets/846fc347c71ada4c01a5a85aabd0722203b84edbafcbe462064ae31d1cf2adbb.png)

A drone is descending toward the ground. The graph of its height $H(t)$, in meters, after $t$ minutes is shown above. Approximate the rate of change of the height at $t=9$ using a forward difference with step size $h=2.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint*: Assume that the rate of change is negative if the height decreases.

After $9$ minutes, the rate of change of the height is {{field-1}} meters per minute.
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the forward difference approximation

$$
{H}^{′}(t)≈\frac{H(t+h)-H(t)}{h},
$$

at the time $t=9$ with step size $h=2.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}^{′}(9) & ≈\frac{H(9+2)-H(9)}{2} \\  & =\frac{H(11)-H(9)}{2} \\  & =\frac{0-80}{2} \\  & =-40.\end{aligned}
$$

So, after $9$ minutes, the rate of change of the height is $-40$ meters per minute.
